_comment: Copy to ~/.claude/speak-config.json. Run scripts-macos/speak-voices.sh to see what this machine actually has. Every field is optional; omitting one keeps its default. Keys beginning with an underscore are documentation and are ignored.
_engine: voiceover | say | auto  (auto = VoiceOver if it is running, else say)
_voice: A say voice name, from speak-voices.sh's 'match' field. Empty means the machine's default Spoken Content voice, which is a fine answer rather than a missing one. IGNORED for voiceover, which has no voice setting by design - it speaks in whatever voice VoiceOver is already configured with, and follows automatically if you change it.
_rate: say: words per minute, roughly 90 to 720. null = the say default of 175. Fast-speech users tend to land between 300 and 450. IGNORED for voiceover, deliberately - rate there is your own VoiceOver setting, and overriding a choice you already made is an accessibility defect.
_interrupt: Whether a new reply cuts off the previous one still speaking. Applies to the say route. On voiceover it does nothing - VoiceOver speaks in its own process and owns its own queue, so your silence key is the control there.
_content: What actually gets spoken. Only Claude's own prose is ever read - thinking, tool calls, tool output and subagent chatter are never spoken regardless of these settings, and only the newest reply is read.

content._codeBlocks: announce (say 'Code block omitted') | omit (skip silently) | read (speak the code)
content._urls: link (say the word 'link') | omit | read (speak the whole URL)
content._firstParagraphOnly: Speak only the opening paragraph. Good for long replies you will read yourself.
content._maxChars: Stop after this many characters and say 'Response truncated'. 0 = no limit.
